newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end sharply lower, PolyGram tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end sharply lower, PolyGram tumbles.

text.p: Dutch shares tumbled on Wednesday in their biggest one-day fall since the end of July as a stuttering Wall Street and subdued dollar was accentuated by domestic corporate jitters.
The market was hit by a profits warning from music and film group PolyGram, which sent its own shares spiralling downwards and dented those of its 75-percent majority parent, Philips.

Another weak start to U.S. stocks on Wednesday was enough to push the AEX index down further in late trade. It ended 9.54 points, or 1.61 percent, down to close at 583.57, near the low for the day at 583.27.
Dealers said general volumes were thin, which partly accounted for the volatilitity and said many large investors were standing aside until the perceived correction had ended.
But the mood was described as positive and fresh inflows of funds were expected once the market had found a bottom. Some thought the correction was already overdone.
Comments from Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing that German interest rates were at a historic low and "nothing more is to be expected or necessary" also had an impact.
Dealers said the comments dented bond sentiment which then spilled over into the stock market.
PolyGram sent a shiver through the market early, saying its full-year operating profit would be flat or just below 1995's. It also announced a one-off $90 million restructuring charge.

The shares slipped in brisk trade, ending 5.40 guilders, or 6.4 percent, lower at 79.50. Analysts said the company possibly face a more prolonged period of stagnation, adding that further restructuring may be necessary.

The announcement had a knock-on effect on 75-percent owned parent Philips, which closed down 2.40 guilders at 56.60. The company reports its third quarter results tomorrow and analysts are also braced for a large restucturing charge.
Elsewhere in the index, oil giant Royal Dutch succumbed to some profit-taking following the recent strong gains.
Dutch PTT, KPN, ended just 0.50 guilders lower at 60.20 as it shrugged of the impact the award of two terrestrial telecoms licences to operators EnerTel and Telfort in the next month.
The two operators will provide competition to the current fixed-line monopoly of Dutch PTT.
